correctness.rationale: Exact equation with A=σ(p^a),B=σ(q^b), U=A-p^a=σ(p^{a-1}), V=B-q^b=σ(q^{b-1}) rearranges to UV=p^a q^b. Congruences U≡1 mod p and V≡1 mod q rule out p=q and force, if p≠q, U=q^b,V=p^a (a=b=1 boundaries also impossible). Substituting U=(p^a−1)/(p−1), V=(q^b−1)/(q−1) gives (p−1)(q−1)p^{a−1}=p^{a−1}−1, impossible. Independently exhaustively checked 22,500 ordered prime/exponent combinations p,q<100, a,b≤6 with exact σ; finite check corroborative only.

value.rationale: This is a complete, unrestricted structure theorem for the most elementary nontrivial prime-support slice of a class introduced for abundant/divisor-sum arithmetic. It proves simultaneous one-prime support is impossible while a previously characterized adjacent mixed-support slice has actual Mersenne-prime solutions, giving a mathematically motivated sharp boundary. The prime-support forcing and coupled geometric-sum contradiction are more than an arbitrary single numerical computation; the scope and limitations are explicit.

final_claim: No harmonious pair (x,y) satisfying x/sigma(x)+y/sigma(y)=1 has x=p^a and y=q^b with primes p,q and integers a,b≥1.
limitations: No one-member prime-power exclusion proved; the theorem requires both members individually prime powers.
